value.reasoning: STRAT_A delivers positive risk-adjusted returns on the two longest windows (384-bar Sharpe 1.79, 24-bar 20.3). STRAT_B shows negative Sharpe on those same windows (-1.22 and -5.03). The strong negative correlation (-0.86) would normally favour a paired allocation, but STRAT_B's persistent negative edge on the long horizon makes it a drag. Removing STRAT_B eliminates the drag and avoids turnover costs from rebalancing a losing leg. Equal-weight fallback applies only when no edge exists; here STRAT_A's long-window Sharpe > 1.5 provides clear evidence.
